generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology you learn the conventions by reading journal articles as a writer, not only for their findings. Read a well-regarded paper a second time and watch how it is made: the introduction, method, results and discussion structure, the hedging of every claim, the impersonal voice, and the way earlier studies are cited to build an argument. These recurring choices are the conventions, and noticing them lets you write towards them rather than waiting to be told the rules.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students are each handed an unfamiliar journal article and asked how writing is done in the field.

Tom reads it once, for content, and reports what the study found. Asked about its conventions, he can only say it was 'formal and quite hard'. The article has been read, but only as information. Its conventions stayed invisible, because he never looked at how it was written.

Amara reads it twice. The second time she ignores the findings and watches the writing: the writer rarely appears, claims are hedged and tied to data, the sections follow a fixed order, and earlier studies are woven into the argument rather than listed. She can now name four conventions of psychology writing and write towards them.

Both students read the same article. Only Amara read it as a writer, and so could see the conventions Tom missed.
generatedProse.summary: Psychology's conventions are learned by reading its articles as a writer: reading a paper again for how it is made, noticing the structure, hedging, impersonal voice and use of studies, and writing towards them. You can now explain that way of reading, appraise an article against the aspects that reveal its conventions, and choose what to notice in an unfamiliar paper. The final lesson puts this to work on writing with a critical edge.

check.body: In the worked example, why could Amara name psychology's conventions when Tom could not?

items.text: She read the article a second time, watching the writing rather than the findings.
She already knew more about the topic than Tom.
She found the article easier to understand.
She agreed with the study's conclusions.

feedback.correct: That's right. A second reading focused on how the article was written made psychology's conventions visible.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what Amara DID differently with the article.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara could name the conventions because she read the article again, watching how it was written rather than what it found.
